title: Vacate and tenancy scope
audience: Home-based property managers and property manager partner workers who may be asked to handle a vacate or tenancy end
learningOutcomes: Identify which vacate tasks are within a property manager partner's scope and which belong to the owner or a licensed professional.
Describe the evidence needed at a vacate without making tenancy decisions.
Refer tenancy, bond and leasing questions and record the referral.

instruction.heading: Separate work from decisions
instruction.body: A vacate involves physical work, such as checking the condition of the property, arranging keys, and organising repairs and cleaning. It also involves decisions: what counts as damage, what is deducted, whether a notice was correctly given, and what the outgoing occupant is responsible for. The second group belongs to the owner, and in many cases to a licensed or regulated process. A property manager partner records the condition and arranges work the owner has approved. Do not make tenancy decisions or promise an outcome to the outgoing occupant.

instruction.heading: Refer tenancy and leasing questions
instruction.body: Questions about notices, rent, bonds, leasing, and tenancy rights should be referred to the owner and to the relevant state authority or qualified professional. The licence position differs by state. In New South Wales, the NSW licence page for real estate agents says a licence is needed to lease and manage property for clients, and that rent collection falls within it (page last modified 20 October 2026). In Queensland, a current resident letting agent licence is required for that work, and its scope is set out on the licence page (last updated 26 October 2026). Record each question, the person it was referred to, and the date. Do not give legal or tenancy advice that the course does not cover.

procedure: Confirm the owner's written instruction for the vacate, including which tasks are approved.
Record the condition of the property against the intake record, with dated photographs.
Arrange approved repairs and cleaning, and record each task and its status.
Refer any tenancy, notice, bond or leasing question to the owner and record the referral.
Do not promise an outcome to the outgoing occupant on any tenancy matter.
Record the handover of keys and the close of the vacate.

workedExamples.situation: An outgoing occupant asks you whether the bond will be returned in full, and whether damage to a wall will be deducted.
workedExamples.reasoning: Do not promise an outcome. Say that the owner makes the decision on the bond and any deduction, and record the question and the referral. Offer the condition evidence from intake and the vacate inspection, and tell the owner that the question has been raised.

commonErrors.error: Promising a bond refund or a deduction to the outgoing occupant.
commonErrors.prevention: Refer the decision to the owner and record the referral.

commonErrors.error: Giving tenancy advice outside the course content.
commonErrors.prevention: Refer tenancy, notice and rent questions to the owner and the relevant authority.

commonErrors.error: Doing approved work without recording its approval.
commonErrors.prevention: Record each task with the owner's written approval.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Real estate and property management licensing differs by state. The New South Wales and Queensland positions are summarised in and. Do not begin leasing or tenancy management until the position for the property's state has been checked on the official page.

Tenancy, notice and bond rules are set by state law. The regulators are NSW Fair Trading, Consumer Affairs Victoria and the Residential Tenancies Authority in Queensland. Victoria caps a bond at one month's rent and requires payment to the RTBA within ten working days of receipt (page last updated 8 December 2025). Queensland caps a bond at four weeks' rent and requires lodgement with the RTA within 10 days, by the owner or property manager (no page date shown). Notice periods are not set out in this course and must be confirmed with the regulator.
Completing this lesson does not give a real estate licence, a tenancy authority or any right to make decisions on bonds or notices.

qualityStandard: Every vacate task has the owner's written approval before it starts.
Every tenancy question is referred and recorded, with no outcome promised.
Condition at vacate is compared with the intake record.
documentationEvidence: Written owner instruction for the vacate
Referral record for each tenancy, notice or bond question
Vacate condition record compared with intake
summary: Physical vacate work is separate from tenancy decisions, which belong to the owner.
Refer tenancy, bond and leasing questions and promise no outcome.
Record approvals and compare the vacate condition with the intake record.

knowledgeChecks.question: An outgoing occupant asks whether their bond will be refunded in full. What is correct?
options: Promise a full refund, since the bond has been paid in full already by the tenant today
Tell them the bond is always returned in full at the end of every lease term
Refer the decision to the owner and record the referral without promising an outcome
Deduct an amount without asking the owner, since the owner is paid by the tenant

knowledgeChecks.question: Which statement about leasing and property management licensing is correct for this course?
options: It is confirmed as not required in every state and territory of the country at all times
It is confirmed as required in every state and territory across the whole country today
It is covered by the handyman licence held by the property manager on the staff team today
It differs by state, so the position for the property's state must be checked before leasing begins

knowledgeChecks.question: Which part of a vacate does the lesson say belongs to the owner or a licensed process?
options: Checking the condition of the property
Deciding what counts as damage and what is deducted
